chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Khashshāb, from Ibn Samāʿah, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said:

I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “The twelve Imams from the family of Muḥammad (عليهم السلام), all of them are muḥaddath, from the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and from the offspring of ʿAlī; and the Messenger of Allah and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) are the two fathers.”

Then ʿAlī ibn Rāshid said: “There was a brother of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn through his mother, and he denied that.” So Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) became stern and said: “Indeed, the son of your mother was one of them.”

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muḥammad, referring to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الِاثْنَا عَشَرَ: the twelve, referring to the number of the Imams
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, meaning the divinely designated leader
key_terms.مُحَدَّثٌ: one spoken to or inspired, i.e. addressed by the angels without prophethood
key_terms.وُلْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the offspring of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the twelve Imams being from the family of Muḥammad and ʿAlī?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the doctrine of the twelve Imams from the family of Muḥammad (عليهم السلام), describing them as muḥaddath and as descendants of both the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and ʿAlī (عليه السلام). It also emphasizes the special paternal status of the Messenger of Allah and ʿAlī (عليه السلام), reinforcing the creedal significance of lineage and Imamate in the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Khashhab, from Ibn Sama’at, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Bin Ribat, from Ibn Azina, from Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The twelve Imams<sup>asws</sup> are from the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, all of them being Muhaddath (whom the Angels discuss with), from the children of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and from the children of Ali<sup>asws</sup>; and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and Ali<sup>asws</sup>, they are the two fathers<sup>asws</sup>’.

Ali Bin Rashid said, ‘There was a brother of Ali Bin Al Husayn<sup>asws</sup> to his<sup>asws</sup> mother’s side, and he denied that, so Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was furious and said: ‘But the son<sup>asws</sup> of your mother is one of them<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn Muhammad al-Khashshab from ibn Sama‘a from Ali ibn al-Hassan ibn Ribat from ibn ’Udhayna from Zurara who has said the following.

“I heard abu Ja‘far say, ‘The twelve Imams all from the family of Muhammad (s.a) are the ones to whom (the angles) speak. They all are from the descendants of the Messenger of Allah and the descendants of Ali the Messenger of Allah and Ali (a.s.) are their ancestors.”

Ali ibn Rashid has said that Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) had a brother from his (foster mother’s / not his real mother the Persian princes) side who did not believe in the Hadith expressed denial. The Imam (a.s.) said to him loudly, “The son of your mother is one of them..”
